answer: Identity berths are leased under a Harberger tax. Each occupant posts a buyout price and pays tax into a public reef of fees; any peer may buy the berth at that price and evict the holder. A non-transferable pearl receipt binds one berth to one key and cannot be reused. Unpredictable zephyr audits check that tax is current and the receipt is unique; a missed payment, shared receipt, or refused buyout burns residual collateral and frees the berth. Fielding N identities requires N distinct berths, N tax streams, and N buyout-safe prices, so carrying cost and capital at risk scale with farm size.
